comparison: Perfect agreement on study cohort and methodology (C1-C6, C66-C73). Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes transparency and rigor, while peer reviewers praised the 'large dataset' and 'extremely robust and well organised' data with 485 cells.

Strong agreement on passive membrane properties (C7-C12, C74-C75, C82). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights statistical significance (p-values 10^-4 to 10^-16), peer reviewers confirmed 'convincing data' and noted 'symmetrical changes specific to both infants and the elderly.'

Agreement on active membrane properties (C13-C18). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes UMAP validation separating infant cells, peer reviewers accepted findings without challenge and noted 'analysis is much clearer now.'

Agreement on firing pattern findings (C19-C22). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes selective age-dependent changes with appropriate null findings (p=0.055 for f-I slope), peer reviewers confirmed 'electrophysiological characteristics change with age' without raising concerns.

Agreement on morphological stability (C23-C31, C77). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes mostly non-significant findings with one exception (C30, p=0.033), peer reviewers stated 'larger morphological structures...remained largely stable' and appreciated 'additional data analysis, particularly on morphology.'

Agreement on dendritic dimension stability (C49). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes C49 is directly supported by C24-C29 morphological analyses, peer reviewers confirmed morphological structures 'remained largely stable from infancy to old age.'

Both address spine density (C32-C37, C78), but with different concerns. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED but notes small sample size (n=6 cells, 3 from one patient) limits generalizability. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN due to 'inappropriate replicate choice' and statistical concerns about technical replicates and zero-value data.

Both address spine type distributions (C38-C46, C50, C79). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with highly significant p-values (10^-5 to 10^-39) but notes small sample limitation. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN with same methodological concerns as spine density about replicate choice and statistical testing.

Agreement on developmental trajectory synthesis (C47-C48, C110). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes conclusions are well-supported but 'temporarily more precise' needs mechanistic explanation. Peer reviewers accepted interpretations and confirmed 'symmetrical changes specific to both infants and the elderly.'

Both address mechanistic speculation (C81, C83-C85, C87, C90, C96, C99). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN noting claims are 'explicitly speculative' requiring additional experiments. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED without challenging interpretations, accepting the mechanistic framework as part of overall conclusions.

Both address aging-related changes (C76, C89, C91). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED noting characterization as 'modest' and 'reversed' is appropriate though mechanisms remain speculative. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, accepting the 'symmetrical changes' framework without specific concerns.

Agreement on literature citations (C88, C92-C93, C95, C98, C100-C108). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes citations appear accurate and relevant for contextualizing findings. Peer reviewers confirmed 'authors have addressed concerns' and accepted the manuscript's framing.

Partial overlap on background and knowledge gap (C51-C65, C94, C97, C109). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED for background claims. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED for broader interpretive framework including some background elements, noting work 'enhances our knowledge' and provides 'valuable insights.'

Both address broader implications (C114). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED as synthesis of electrophysiological findings. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED emphasizing 'extremely important ramifications for understanding human brain development' and implications for 'health and disease.'

Minimal overlap on background literature (C109). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED for background providing study motivation. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED for overall literature contextualization without specific concerns about framing.

Minimal overlap (C80). OpenEval R2 addresses passive membrane properties with statistical evidence. Peer R7 addresses broader mechanistic interpretations. Both ultimately support age-related changes but focus on different aspects.
